neighbours.label: the name-ending piece after 'Men'/'Menc' in classical names (Menc|ius, Men|o)
fire: Scholars often compare the ethics of Confucius and Mencius on human nature.
According to Mencius, people are born with a tendency toward goodness.
The teachings of Mencius were collected by his students after his death.
In Plato's dialogue, Socrates questions Meno about the nature of virtue.
The Meno raises a famous puzzle about how learning is possible.
Later Confucians treated Mencius as the second sage after Confucius.
Her thesis examines how Mencius argued with rival philosophers.
Students reading the Meno often focus on the slave boy geometry lesson.
quiet: Scholars often compare the ethics of Confucius and Laozi on human nature.
According to Xunzi, people are born with a tendency toward selfishness.
The teachings of Confucius were collected by his students after his death.
In Plato's dialogue, Socrates questions Euthyphro about the nature of piety.
The Republic raises a famous puzzle about justice and happiness.
Later Confucians treated Zhu Xi as a great commentator on the classics.
Her thesis examines how Zhuangzi argued with rival philosophers.
Students reading the Phaedo often focus on the arguments about the soul.
